Definition: from G575 and G236; to change away, i.e. release, (reflexively) remove:--deliver, depart.
BiblicalUsage: To deliver, to depart, to be released. The evil spirits depart from those touched by Paul's handkerchiefs, and Christ came to deliver those who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage. The word is the release itself, the going free.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for deliverance carries no teaching of its own; its hope is Hebrews', that Christ came to free those who lived their whole lives in fear of death.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
